title: Report each adopted runtime-started Claude turn to Engram as an unadmitted turn with its observed checks
outcome: Report each adopted runtime-started Claude turn to Engram as an unadmitted turn with its observed checks
acceptance: When an adopted runtime-started turn ends in a session bound to claimed work, the host sends one execution_observe unadmitted_turn under account_if_eligible, with causality unknown and the exact binding, root basis and capture cut current at its closing capture. host_turn_ref names the adopted turn; the host retains its actual adoption time without treating it as a pre-effect start or admission. observed_interval is the envelope of the reported observations, not the turn's execution duration: its from is the earlier of adoption and the original baseline.observed_at when a content_comparison is included, otherwise adoption; its through is the actual closing observation cut, no earlier than the closing sighting and no later than request construction. Every serialized observation timestamp lies within that interval. The source_change is measured against the previous checkpoint's end basis for the same workspace and binding: content_comparison when the revisions differ, null when they are equal, assumed_missing_baseline when no compatible measured basis exists. The baseline keeps its original revision and measured timestamp. The comparison reports endpoint drift with unknown causality; it does not attribute pre-adoption changes to the adopted turn or assert continuous observation of the intervening gap. It is never sent as turn_evaluate, turn_begin or a checkpoint, and never under another turn's grant. A test drives a runtime-started turn with an edit through the production frame router and shows the request and its accounted receipt, including a baseline observed before adoption.

Each test run the turn observed is sent once as an uncredited ObservedCheck with its own stable host_check_id. Up to 16 travel inside the unadmitted_turn, the rest as standalone observed_check occurrences of the same host_turn_ref. The local 64-entry cap on unassigned observations never truncates what is sent to Engram (Engram's no-truncation rule). A test with 70 observed runs shows each reaches the producer exactly once and none is credited.

The pending report is saved with the session before it is sent. Its idempotency key derives from the host turn ref, plus the check id for a standalone check. A lost reply or a restart resends the identical request. A definitive refusal ends in a visible host diagnostic naming the code, never a silent drop or a retry loop. Tests cover a lost reply (identical resend, one record), a restart before the reply (identical resend), and a refusal (diagnostic).
In a session with no claimed work binding, nothing is sent, and the turn's transcript notice says the turn is not reported to Engram. A test shows it.
The full gate passes on the exact committed tree.
